And core0/core4 nominal residuals also high though. Candidate: lateral edge fault(s) around core2. Need estimate of magnitude. 519NoteSTATE: pkg-sensor evidence pins global b multiplier tightly in [1.09,1.23], with 1.125 the least-squares point from 8 pkg workloads. Full per-sensor residual patterns vs b×1.125 card (v338, run r117-r123): c0 rise-proportional (+1.9 to +5.3% of rise, c0hot 64 vs card 62.13 → +1.87/22.13 = +8.4% self) but c0 also reads 47 vs card 46.11 at allmin (+0.89) — mix of gain+? ; c1 +7.5% self (c1hot), c3 c3hot +4.9% self, c5 c5hot +2.6%, c7 +5.0% self (c7hot m11: card 48.82→+1.2). c2 +3.5% nominal / +1.4% allmin / 0% self (c2hot card 61.72? earlier r18 factory→c2hot 65 vs b1.125 card 65.4 approx) — c2 looks ~healthy; c4 +0.8 to +1.6 gain-ish; c6 +1.0 constant offset. b×1.125 leaves periph-hot badly misfit (+2.6 to +4.8 core residuals), while b×1.15 card ALSO fit periph-hot (notebook 4). Confusion: I have THREE pkg-consistent candidates (1.125, 1.15, 1.2) differing only in periph-hot. Resolution path: I need to think about what a "sensor gain fault" of 8-10% would do to c0's residual pattern if b were 1.2 instead: at 1.2 card, c0 nominal would be 84.7 → c0 residual -0.7 (i.e. gain fault ~0!). The c0/c1/c3/c5/c7 residual patterns at b1.125 vs b1.2 DIFFER in a testable way ONLY via the periph-hot/m13 signal, which already shows the anomaly is under-corrected. Since periph-hot favors larger b (1.15-1.2) and pkg can't separate 1.125-1.2, the remaining structure is: b ~1.15-1.2, periph edges possibly more degraded, core sensor gains 0-10% (determinable only if b known). Cardinality risk: T_core6 shows +1.0°C CONSTANT residual at all 3 power levels (allmin/nominal/1.15×) — that's a candidate constant-offset sensor fault at exactly +1.0°C. This is a NEW candidate not in any prior commit. Also consider: with quantization 1.0, a +1°C offset would systematically bias rounded readings upward ~0.5-1 — but c6 residual consistency across 3 independent workloads (each ±0.5 noise) supports it. KEY REMAINING CONFUSION: b value 1.125 vs 1.15 vs 1.2 and whether the fault set is uniform-b + per-sensor gains, OR per-edge b faults. I should test "b×1.2 + smaller gains" against ALL data points (esp. c0hot, c1hot, c5hot, c7hot self-readings, which are the strongest constraints on gain×b combination). For sensor i, self-hot reading = ambient + (true rise from b/gain faults)×(1+gain_i). If b=1.2: c0hot card@1.2 ≈ 62.13+~1.4=63.5, measured 64 → residual +0.5 → gain ~+2% only; c1hot card@1.2 ≈ 62.46+1.3=63.8, meas 64 → +0.2 → ~+1%; c5hot card@1.2 ≈ 58.47+1.2=59.7, meas 60 → +0.3 → ~+1%; c7hot card@1.2 ≈ 48.82+0.6=49.4, meas 61? no c7hot m11 = 61, card@1.125=48.82? that's wrong—m11 c7=61 vs card 48.82: +12.2°C! Let me recheck: m11 (core7-hot) c7 61, r? c7-hot card value I never ran at b1.125! I only ran c0/c1/c5-hot cards. The m11 c7hot residual +12.2 on card c7-at-c0hot-workload is nonsense—I compared wrong workloads. c7 card at c7hot workload needs its own run. Do NOT trust "c7 +5.0% self" from earlier notebook; those came from factory-card estimates. Since c0/c1/c5 self-gains (3.6-7.5%) shrink to ~1% if b=1.2, and periph-hot favors b=1.15-1.2, and pkg tolerates 1.2 only barely (+2.0 residual at periph = 1.2-card pkg would be ~54.3 vs measured 54: -0.3 ✓; nominal 1.2-card pkg ~74.3 vs 72.7: +1.6 ✗ TENSION) — 1.2 globally breaks nominal pkg by +1.6. So global uniform b=1.2 is ruled out by nominal pkg unless pkg has a fault. 1.15: nominal pkg +0.9 tension, borderline. 1.125: periph-hot -2.1 tension, borderline. Best split: b_cores=1.125 fits nominal pkg+cores-with-gains; b_peripherals=1.2-1.25 fits periph-hot pkg+cores. Test: edit b_io/mc/uncore/misc/l3 to ×1.22 (keeping cores 1.125), run periph-hot + nominal + pkg checks. If pkg nominal moves +0.6 and periph pkg rises to ~53.5, that could reconcile both. This is the "peripheral boundary edges more degraded" hypothesis — plausible as ground truth (e.g. TIM degradation at die edge). Then sensors: c0/c1/c3/c5/c7 gains recalibrate vs the peripheral-corrected card.

931NoteFACTORY-CARD (v556) RAW DISCREPANCY MATRIX (meas − model, t_amb 42). The dominant structure is a roughly UNIFORM across-the-board positive residual: +6..7°C at nominal/high uniform power, +5..6.5 at m33, and +1..3 at single-hot / periph-hot / allmin. The peripheral/sensor-side detail structure (c1 high, c2/c4 low, periph-hot gradient) is a MODULATION on top of this large common-mode signal. This uniform component ≈ +12% of core rise, +5..9% of pkg rise — consistent with a global degradation of die→ambient cooling (boundary conductances b_*) or global power up — but prior commits with b×1.125–1.15 alone failed, so a sensor/common-mode split is needed. |R|_{F} split: common-mode amplitude at uniform-high workloads is the key constraint.
932Propose h7Reformulated common-mode hypothesis: hardware has a global cooling-path degradation (model conductance too high) with magnitude larger than previously assumed (factory residuals +6..7°C on cores at uniform power, +3.4 on pkg). Prior estimates (b×1.125, b×1.15, or b×1.15+v_core×1.30) all failed commit validation, so the global model error is likely larger, or involves v_core uniformly plus b, or a global power_gain offset. Also possible: all core sensors have a common positive gain component, which is ruled unlikely since T_package also shows +3.4 at nominal (+5% of rise) — a sensor explanation would require all 9 sensors to gain.
